es: Revisar un párrafo de opinión equilibrando reforzadores (clearly, undeniably) y matizadores (arguably, it would seem, tend to) según la evidencia disponible.

teaching.en: Remote work is undeniably popular: the survey shows that most employees prefer it.
teaching.es: El trabajo a distancia es innegablemente popular: la encuesta muestra que la mayoría de los empleados lo prefiere.
teaching.explanationEs: Undeniably es un reforzador: úsalo solo si la evidencia es sólida, como una encuesta amplia.
segments: Remote work is undeniably popular: the survey
shows that most employees prefer it.
teaching.audioText: Remote work is undeniably popular: the survey shows that most employees prefer it.

teaching.en: Remote work is arguably more productive, but the evidence is still limited.
teaching.es: El trabajo a distancia es, podría decirse, más productivo, pero la evidencia aún es limitada.
teaching.explanationEs: Arguably es un matizador: se puede defender la idea, sin afirmarla del todo.
segments: Remote work is arguably more productive,
but the evidence is still limited.
teaching.audioText: Remote work is arguably more productive, but the evidence is still limited.

teaching.en: It would seem that students tend to learn somewhat better in the morning.
teaching.es: Parece ser que los estudiantes suelen aprender algo mejor por la mañana.
teaching.explanationEs: It would seem, tend to y somewhat suavizan la afirmación; con tres a la vez, uno bastaría.
segments: It would seem that students tend to
learn somewhat better in the morning.
teaching.audioText: It would seem that students tend to learn somewhat better in the morning.

teaching.en: Some critics exaggerate the problem when they say that nobody reads books anymore.
teaching.es: Algunos críticos exageran el problema cuando dicen que ya nadie lee libros.
teaching.explanationEs: Nobody, always y never suelen exagerar: sustitúyelos por many, often o tend to.
segments: Some critics exaggerate the problem when they
say that nobody reads books anymore.
teaching.audioText: Some critics exaggerate the problem when they say that nobody reads books anymore.

teaching.en: The report is too timid: it should say that the cost is unquestionably higher.
teaching.es: El informe es demasiado tímido: debería decir que el coste es sin lugar a dudas más alto.
teaching.explanationEs: También hay exceso de cautela: si la evidencia es clara, hay que reforzar.
segments: The report is too timid: it should
say that the cost is unquestionably higher.
teaching.audioText: The report is too timid: it should say that the cost is unquestionably higher.

teaching.en: The new rule has arguably improved attendance, at least to some extent.
teaching.es: La nueva norma ha mejorado, podría decirse, la asistencia, al menos hasta cierto punto.
teaching.explanationEs: To some extent limita el alcance: no toda la mejora se debe a la norma.
segments: The new rule has arguably improved
attendance, at least to some extent.
teaching.audioText: The new rule has arguably improved attendance, at least to some extent.

prompt.es: Elige la versión más ajustada a la evidencia.

choices.text: Many students tend to dislike homework.

feedback.es: Many y tend to describen una tendencia; all, always y nobody exageran una generalización.

origin.text: Afirmación inicial: «Todos los estudiantes siempre odian los deberes.»

prompt.es: Completa: «El 90 % está de acuerdo: el plan es innegablemente popular.»

feedback.es: Con pruebas sólidas (una encuesta amplia) se puede reforzar con undeniably.

hint.es: La evidencia es sólida: elige un reforzador.

origin.text: The survey shows that 90 percent agree, so the plan is ___ popular.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Podría decirse que es el mejor plan.»

answer.text: It is arguably the best plan

feedback.es: Arguably suaviza un superlativo que es defendible pero discutible.

prompt.es: Completa: «Los estudiantes suelen aprender mejor por la mañana.»

feedback.es: Tend to + verbo base expresa una tendencia, no una regla sin excepciones.

origin.text: Students ___ to learn better in the morning.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige por qué usa un reforzador.

choices.text: Because he is not sure about it.
Because the data support the claim.

feedback.es: Unquestionably está justificado porque los datos muestran viajes veinte minutos más cortos.

origin.audio: I think the new bus route is unquestionably better. The data show that journeys are twenty minutes shorter.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada expresión con su función.

feedback.es: Undeniably refuerza; arguably, it would seem y somewhat matizan en distinto grado.

prompt.es: Revisa el borrador (unas 100 palabras): modera 4 exageraciones y refuerza 2 cautelas.

answer.text: Phones are arguably the biggest distraction in many classrooms, but they are not the only problem. Students tend to learn better without them, although the evidence is somewhat limited. The new ban will probably help, but it would seem that it cannot solve every problem. The survey of two hundred teachers clearly shows that 85 percent support the rule. Attendance has undeniably improved: it is ten percent higher than three years ago. Teachers say there are fewer interruptions, but that is only their opinion. To some extent, the ban explains this change, but we should keep measuring the results.
accepted: Phones are arguably the biggest distraction in many classrooms, but they are not the only problem. Students tend to learn better without them, although the evidence is somewhat limited. The new ban will probably help, but it would seem that it cannot solve every problem. The survey of two hundred teachers clearly shows that 85 percent support the rule. Attendance has undeniably improved: it is ten percent higher than three years ago. Teachers say there are fewer interruptions, but that is only their opinion. To some extent, the ban explains this change, but we should keep measuring the results.

Phones are arguably the main distraction in many schools, but they are not the only one. It would seem that students learn better without them, although the evidence is limited. The ban will probably help, but it cannot solve every problem. The survey of 200 teachers clearly shows that 85 percent support it. Attendance has unquestionably improved, because it is ten percent higher than three years ago. Many teachers say lessons are calmer, but we have no data about that. To some extent, the ban explains the change, so we should keep checking the results.

Phones are one of the biggest distractions in classrooms, but not the only one. Students tend to learn better without them, although we only have opinions. The ban may help, but it would seem that it cannot solve every problem. The survey of two hundred teachers undeniably shows that most support the rule: 85 percent agree. Attendance is clearly better, ten percent higher than three years ago. Teachers say lessons are calmer, although that is only an opinion, so we should not exaggerate. To some extent, the ban explains this, but we need more data.

feedback.es: El párrafo revisado modera las exageraciones con arguably, tend to o it would seem y refuerza con clearly o undeniably lo que la encuesta y la asistencia sí demuestran.

origin.text: Borrador: «Phones are the worst thing in schools. Everybody knows that students never learn anything with a phone. The new ban will solve every problem. Perhaps, maybe, the survey could possibly suggest that teachers are happy. It is maybe possible that attendance is a little better.» Datos: la encuesta a 200 profesores muestra que el 85 % apoya la norma (prueba sólida); la asistencia subió un 10 % en tres años (prueba sólida); sobre el aprendizaje solo hay opiniones (prueba parcial). Reescribe el párrafo en unas 100 palabras.

prompt.es: Elige la frase mejor ajustada a una encuesta de solo doce personas.

choices.text: It would seem that the new library suits many people.
The new library is undeniably perfect for everyone.
The new library is surely the best in the country.

feedback.es: Con doce opiniones solo se puede matizar (it would seem, many); undeniably, perfect y everyone exageran.

origin.text: Un artículo dice que la nueva biblioteca es perfecta para todos, pero la encuesta solo incluye a doce personas.

prompt.es: Completa: «innegablemente claras» y «podría decirse que su mejor obra».

feedback.es: Las cifras son una prueba sólida (reforzador); que sea su mejor obra es discutible (matizador).

sentences: The figures are ___ clear: sales fell by half.
The film is ___ his best work, but not everyone agrees.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Los adolescentes suelen dormir algo menos de lo necesario.»

answer.text: Teenagers tend to sleep somewhat less than they need

feedback.es: Tend to y somewhat matizan una generalización sobre los adolescentes.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué hace el hablante con la enfermedad de la dueña.

choices.text: He saw the owner in bed.

feedback.es: Presumably marca una suposición: el hablante no ha hablado con la dueña.

origin.audio: I have not spoken to the owner, but presumably she is ill. The shop is closed today.

prompt.es: Elige la frase que marca esa información de segunda mano.

feedback.es: Apparently indica que la información viene de otra fuente y no está comprobada; evidently y undoubtedly la afirman con seguridad.

origin.text: Tu amigo dice que el director dimitió, pero solo lo has leído en un blog.

prompt.es: Completa: «Según informan, la empresa ha perdido mucho dinero.»

feedback.es: Reportedly se coloca tras el auxiliar y marca que la información viene de la prensa.

origin.text: The company has ___ lost a lot of money.
